$meta.purpose: Per-cert LINEAGE declaration registry for every NUMERICAL-CORRECTNESS certificate (fold-numeric / kernel byte-exact / repack-numeric). Consumed by tools/lint/check_cert_requirements.py, which fails CLOSED unless each cert declares -- and its declaration internally satisfies -- the THREE CERT REQUIREMENTS (G3-cert-hardening 裁决, 防复发入宪). Motivated by the M2c 误诊: a q4_K repack-GEMM 'byte-exact' claim backed by (1) a row-quant oracle against a mat-quant/interleaved dispatch (wrong input path) and (2) a self-comparing / shared-impl reference (hollow certificate) -- neither of which the corpus ever exercised the dmin-term against. See docs/reports/2026-07-09-minterm-fold-audit.md §3 for the adjudication 判据 (a)-(d) this schema encodes, and docs/reports/2026-07-09-zero-model-adjudication-method.md for the terminal ZERO-MODEL rule.
$meta.requirement_rule: claim=full  <=>  (①corpus complete: every arithmetic term of the fold is EXERCISED, none merely declared) AND (②input path same-origin: oracle quantizer == tested-dispatch quantizer AND the tested path is the real dispatch, link-by-link) AND (③oracle independent: the reference does NOT share the被测物's read implementation -- self-compare PRE≡POST / untiled≡tiled / shared-impl is NOT an independent oracle). A cert that cannot meet all three must lower its claim to 'partial' (and DECLARE the gap) or stand as a 'failure' (falsification) cert. Undeclared / self-compare-masquerading-as-independent / corpus-gap-not-marked-partial = RED.

claim_semantics.full: asserts NUMERIC CORRECTNESS (byte-exact / 0-mismatch). MUST satisfy all three requirements -- this is the only claim the three-requirement gate hard-enforces.
claim_semantics.partial: asserts correctness only on a DECLARED sub-corpus / with a named caveat (some arithmetic term un-exercised, or input path not dispatch-faithful, or oracle not independent). Allowed to carry gaps -- but must still DECLARE the fold's full required-term set so the gap is visible.
claim_semantics.failure: a FALSIFICATION cert: it demonstrated the被测物 is WRONG. One-sided evidence -- any corpus that triggers a mismatch is valid, so the strong corpus/same-origin/independence bars are not hard-enforced (a defect found on a narrow corpus is still a real defect).

oracle_independence_semantics.independent: reference recomputed by an implementation that does NOT share the被测物's read/fold code (e.g. a per-element scalar oracle). The ONLY value that may back a claim=full.
oracle_independence_semantics.self-compare: reference is the被测物 in another configuration: PRE≡POST, untiled≡tiled, S1≡S6, golden≡variant. Proves an invariant (order/tiling preservation), NOT absolute correctness -- both sides can carry the SAME defect (M2c proved S1 and S6 were BOTH wrong yet self-compared 0-mismatch).
oracle_independence_semantics.shared-impl: an 'independent' harness that nonetheless reuses the被测物's bsums/fold read layout, so it cannot see a defect in that shared code (the hollow #6/#11 certs).

corpus_term_semantics.dmin_nonzero: super-block min offset x->dmin != 0 (the min-TERM is actually activated; a dmin=0 corpus never exercises the min fold).
corpus_term_semantics.mins_nonzero: per-sub-block mins[] not all zero (non-degenerate min).
corpus_term_semantics.nondegenerate_scale: block scale d not unit/degenerate (int regime d=dmin=1.0 does NOT count).
corpus_term_semantics.second_scale_nonzero: the 2nd scale plane exercised (q5_K qh 5th-bit plane / dual d,dmin).
corpus_term_semantics.sign_coverage_signed: activations span negative AND positive (ri8 -127..127 class).
corpus_term_semantics.codebook_full_index: IQ codebook index space exercised beyond a trivial entry.
corpus_term_semantics.superblock_boundary: accumulation crosses a sub-block / super-block boundary (interleaving / carry exercised).

$meta.fold_model_note: Each cert declares the fold_model of the被测物. Its corpus_terms.required MUST be a SUPERSET of fold_model_required_terms[fold_model] -- a cert may not narrow away a mandatory arithmetic term of the fold it certifies (that is exactly how the min-term hollow certs escaped: they omitted dmin_nonzero from what they exercised). fold_model_required_terms and corpus_term_vocab are a CONTROLLED vocabulary: extend them deliberately (and log in schema/VERSIONLOG.md) when onboarding a new fold family; an entry naming an unknown fold_model or corpus term is RED (typo / undeclared guard).
$meta.input_path_lineage_note: tested_quantizer = the activation quantizer on the REAL被测 dispatch (mat-quant e.g. ggml_quantize_mat_q8_K_4x1 vs row-quant e.g. quantize_row_q8_K). oracle_quantizer = the quantizer feeding the REFERENCE. For claim=full they MUST be equal (same-origin) AND dispatch_faithful MUST be true (the被测 path is the production dispatch, not an isolated harness). The M2c 误诊 = row-quant oracle vs mat-quant/interleaved dispatch -> this gate would have failed that 'full' claim closed.
$meta.registry_completeness_note: This registry carries the M2c SEED (a FAILURE / falsification cert that ALSO clears the claim=full bar, doubling as the reference lineage) PLUS the M4 DECISIVE full certs (M4-q4K / M4-q5K repack-GEMM, commit 4f765790) that RECOVERED the M2c-narrowed q4_K/q5_K claims: on a REAL dmin!=0 Q4_K_M model tensor, fed the SAME ggml_quantize_mat_q8_K_4x1 q8 both sides, our compiler-emitted repack-GEMM is INTEGER bit-exact (MAIN/MIN 0 mismatch) and is CLOSER to the integer-exact fold than ggml's own generic repack GEMM is -- so the 'min-term VLEN128 bug' was a cert-harness quantizer-mismatch artifact (row-quant/lrintf oracle vs mat-quant dispatch), not a kernel defect. The full back-fill of every K-quant / repack / fold / byte-exact cert into this registry is done by the PARALLEL accounting line, not here. The gate validates whatever is declared; it does NOT scan the filesystem for un-declared certs (roster completeness is the accounting line's ledger, T8). Still OWED (declared partial in T8 [CERT-3REQ], not yet full certs here): the repack-GEVM path and a DIRECT q2_K dmin!=0 cert (q2_K is presently validated only via the M4-proven SHARED kquant_dmin_bsums_min fold).
$meta.frontmatter_alternative: A future variant may inline this declaration as YAML frontmatter inside each cert's MANIFEST.md instead of a central registry; check_cert_requirements.py would then parse frontmatter blocks. The central registry is used first because every other schema/ gate in this repo (frontdoor-provenance, monolith-retire, opponent-facts-pin) reads a central schema/*.v1.json.

certs.note: SEED / reference lineage. The one fully-adequate cert: real ggml_mul_mat interleaved-q8_Kx4 dispatch, dmin!=0 NORM corpus, per-element independent oracle_dot2 (mins += m0*a8). It is a FAILURE cert -- it caught a NUMERIC DIVERGENCE (rel 5%..314% per super-block, per-column R/correct 0.947/0.637 even/odd parity) but MIS-ATTRIBUTED it to a kernel 'min-term defect'. M1 (ZERO-MODEL) then M4 (decisive, vs ggml's OWN generic) reversed that attribution: the kernel is bit-exact to the actual mat-quant dispatch; the divergence was the cert-harness quantizing the activation differently (row-quant/lrintf) from what ggml really feeds the GEMM (generic mat-quant). Its lineage ALSO clears the claim=full bar (all three requirements satisfied), so it doubles as the positive worked example of a compliant declaration. See docs/reports/2026-07-09-minterm-fold-audit.md §3 row 1; the reversal is the M4-q4K/M4-q5K certs below.

certs.op_path: q4_K repack GEMM VLEN128 (kquant_dmin_bsums_min fold) vs ggml's OWN generic + independent int-exact oracle
certs.note: M4 DECISIVE -- CASE CLOSED (commit 4f765790). REAL Q4_K_M model tensor blk.0.attn_k.weight (K=4096,N=1024,nb=16), dmin!=0 = 16384/16384 (min 2.1e-4 .. max 1.1e-2, MIN-TERM ACTIVE), the SAME ggml_quantize_mat_q8_K_4x1 q8 fed to both sides. In-kernel INTEGER MAIN/MIN capture vs recompute-from-mat-quant-q8 = 0/0 mismatches => INTEGER BIT-EXACT. FLOAT: OURS vs independent int-exact oracle max_rel 2.86e-6; OURS vs ggml's OWN ggml_gemm_q4_K_16x1_q8_K_generic max_rel 6.31e-5 (pure FP-reassociation) -- OURS is in fact CLOSER to the integer-exact fold than ggml's own generic is. This RECOVERS the M2c-narrowed q4_K claim: the 'min-term VLEN128 bug' is a cert-harness row-quant/lrintf oracle-mismatch artifact, not a kernel defect. All three requirements met: real mat-quant dispatch (same-origin + dispatch-faithful), dmin!=0 NORM corpus (complete), independent per-element int-exact oracle. See MANIFEST.md / m4_decisive_result.log.
